**US-Iran conflict escalates.** The US bombed Iranian radar sites after Iran targeted American forces in Kuwait, according to [the BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crlpy8n7pr6o). Sirens sounded over Kuwait City following the strikes on Iranian military facilities. Iran's attacks have damaged 20 US military installations since the war began, satellite images show.

**OPEC+ production decision.** The cartel is likely to raise its July oil output target despite disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, [Reuters reports](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/opec-likely-raise-july-oil-output-target-despite-hormuz-disruption-sources-say-2026-06-01/). Shipping through the vital waterway faces continued threats from Iranian naval operations. Asian imports of US crude have surged but cannot fully offset losses from Gulf supply routes.

**Trump brokers partial Lebanon deal.** Israel and Hezbollah accepted a US-proposed reduction in hostilities, though [clashes continue](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c202rxp1z15o) across southern Lebanon. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu faced criticism after Trump halted planned strikes on Beirut suburbs. The partial ceasefire represents Trump's first diplomatic intervention in the conflict.

**Saudi Foreign Minister comments.** Prince Faisal bin Farhan said via Twitter that Saudi Arabia "highly appreciates" Trump's decision to give diplomacy a chance in ending the war and restoring maritime navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. The kingdom expressed support for negotiations to address regional disagreements.

**Saudi Hajj leadership.** Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman received calls from French President Emmanuel Macron and was congratulated by Princess Reema on the successful Hajj season. Prince Khalid bin Salman met with UK National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell to discuss regional challenges and bilateral cooperation.

**Kuwait prison escape.** Three prisoners escaped from a Kuwaiti facility, including two death row inmates and a drug smuggler, [Independent Arabia reports](https://www.independentarabia.com/node/650268/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1/%D9%85%D8%AD%D9%83%D9%88%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A5%D8%B9%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%85-%D9%88%D9%85%D9%87%D8%B1%D8%A8-%D9%85%D8%AE%D8%AF%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%AA%D9%81%D8%A7%D8%B5%D9%8A%D9%84-%D9%87%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%A8-3-%D8%B3%D8%AC%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%82%D8%A8%D8%B6-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%8A%D9%87%D9%85-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%83%D9%88%D9%8A%D8%AA). The three were subsequently apprehended by Kuwaiti authorities. No details were provided on how the escape was carried out or when the arrests occurred.

**Bahrain travel ban.** Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced citizens are prevented from traveling to Iran and Iraq due to ongoing security tensions, according to [Sky News Arabia](https://news.google.-?oc=5). The measure follows heightened regional tensions and affects travel to the two neighboring countries.

**Oman-Libya energy pact.** Oman and Libya signed a memorandum of understanding for joint oil and gas exploration activities, [Times of Oman reports](https://timesofoman.com//article/172501-oman-libya-sign-mou-to-enhance-ties-in-oil-and-gas). The agreement aims to enhance bilateral energy cooperation between the two nations. No financial details or timeline for potential projects were disclosed.

**Saudi financial measures.** The Saudi Interior Ministry seized 845,087 amphetamine tablets hidden in cardboard sheets in the Eastern Region as part of ongoing drug enforcement operations. King Salman also issued a royal order promoting 327 members of the Public Prosecution across various judicial ranks.
